That addresses a meeting with a liaison officer concerning activities in the Cetina valley, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: "To inform Pero [phoen] that tension in Cetina had eased after some Simo requested Karlo [phoen] to use his influence." Yeah, "to stop the shelling." Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Let us go to 1D100537 so we can place ourselves here. If you could just take a look at that, General. This is the map of the Cetina-Grahovo area mid-July 1995. If you can take a look at that Mr. Ermolaev, and you can see the RSK positions as well as the joint RSK positions being in red along a confrontation line and a joint HV/HVO forces in blue to the right.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we move to the centre of that and we point to the centre and we see a box with an X in the middle. That indicates an artillery position in Cetina, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And there also was the -- and that's on behalf of the ARSK. Take your time, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that -- these articles RSK. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you are familiar with the ARSK in dealing with your UNMOs, you are familiar with the ARSK positions that were located in the Cetina valley south of Grahovo and next to the confrontation line with the HV and the HVO; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure that we had such exact and detailed knowledge of any -- of all positions there on any side I can assure you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, but you did have an idea that this was the approximate locations of the warring factions --

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- in late July of 1995, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. I would just like to clarify. When he says that -- that this was the approximate locations, is he asking the witness to confirm that the map is accurate or that the general area he's described was the location of these units?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, may I take it that you're willing to clarify for Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: These are the approximate locations of the various ARSK units in the Cetina valley. The witness said that he didn't know the exact locations, but these were the approximate locations of ARSK units in the Cetina valley.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, if we can have this marked and moved into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask for some foundation of whether or not this is actually accurate. The witness hasn't indicated that the positions, as they're represented on the map, are accurate. I think there has to be some foundation laid for what is -- what this document purports to represent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness said that these are the approximate locations. That will go to weight, not to admissibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, weight or admissibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure if the witness actually adopted this map as the approximate locations. It's my -- I mean, the way I read this transcript he was asking him if the general area of Strmica, Grahovo, and Cetina was the area where these units were located. Not that this map happens to represent where they were located in those areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We scroll back, Your Honour, and go into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you already assign a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit D153.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your objection is denied, Mr. Russo. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ermolaev, in the Cetina valley in late July -- mid to late July of 1995, there was shelling going on both from the RSK to the HV side and the HV side to the ARSK side, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recollect that such reporting I had from UNMOs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let us turn our attention then to -- back to P99, page 8.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What we were reading before on the summaries of the meetings.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could go -- put that back on the screen. And that summary of meeting is at --

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Page 8. Yes, if you can see that. I'm sorry. If you can just -- page 8 of that document, and it begins "Summary of meetings." And just to orient you just a bit, this is 23 July, 1995. And if we could just blow-up, Madam Registrar, that number (3) where it says "Summary of meetings." Do you see that, sir? Do you see that okay? "At 210900 SMO, senior military observer, had a meeting with the chief liaison officer to UN and ECMM in Zadar. SMO was pleased to inform CALO, that's the Croatian army liaison officer, that the tension in Cetina gives the grid reference had eased after SMR requested CALO to use his influence to stop the shelling of civilian targets. The farmers are now harvesting their crops; at the same time, UNMOs patrol the area to ensure that there are no military targets deployed there. However, the shelling on 9 July was an exception in that this could only be regarded as the deliberate targeting of innocent people. CALO replied that "According to their information there were military targets in the area at that time." He also stated that "If the combined Serb/Abdic forces did not halt their attack against Bihac, the Croatian forces would likely have to intervene." Now, the Abdic forces were the forces were operating in conjunction with the Serbs in the Bihac pocket, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the information that you received back, did you receive information that the Serbs had military weaponry in the Cetina valley?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: So to my mind, and it's clearly from this report, and I -- I'm just trying to recollect it, I've never seen a report from UNMOs that they observed military targets in Cetina in those villages where they were monitoring the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, when you wanted to go to the Cetina valley, you did not have freedom of movement when you were operating with the ARSK, did you?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had in July many problems there, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you had to get permission of the ARSK to travel into the Cetina valley, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just don't want to be mistaken, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me help you out then. Why don't you just -- why don't we turn to a sitrep --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kehoe. I waited to intervene to see whether the witness would come with an answer. Your last question, whether you have to get permission, could be understood in a normative way and could be understood in a factual way, and -- you understand what I mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I don't understand the discrepancy. Permission in the context --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, permission is that if you need permission, it can be that the party which gives the permission requires you to ask a permission, although under the normative system applicable at that time they should not ask for that. Then it's a factual situation. So if you ask, "Do you -- do you need the permission of the Italian Mafia to have a restaurant on Sicily, the answer in a normative way would be no. However in a factual situation it might be that you have to get such permission. So that's the difference I was pointing at and that was not clear from your question, whether it was put in a normative way or a factual way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's probably yes in both contexts, Judge, but nevertheless --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It could be. I'm not giving the answers, I'm just analysing your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In the spirit of precision Judge, and using only the words that are used, the reason I picked the word "permission" as opposed to some other maybe appropriate word in whatever context is that it comes -- that particular word comes from the situation report which I'll address now. That's why I picked that word because that was written in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the way in which you used this in your question leaves some discrepancy. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And just to assist you along, let us turn our attention to 65 ter 173. And if I could just go to page 1 first. And I'll just orient you, Mr. Ermolaev. This is a situation report from 4 July 1995. And if we could turn our attention to the top of page 7 in that document. And I don't know if you want to see the prior page, Mr. Ermolaev, because that is summary of meetings, so it's just on the prior page and I'll gladly show you that, but this is a -- at the top of the page the Team Podkonje meeting and the subject of the meeting is "Lifting Restriction of Movement, Security Situation UNMO Team, ARSK Official Stated." "UNMO teams should have freedom of movement in the area -- AOR area of responsibility of 1 Brigade North Dalmatian Corps but to secure their safety there must be a permission from the liaison officer in Knin." So you would agree with me, Mr. Ermolaev, that in July, in order to move into the area of the 1st brigade of the north Dalmatian corps you had to have the permission of the army of the Republic of Serb Krajina, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but regarding July and answering yes, I mean we had general deterioration with the freedom of movement, I mean, in this side as well. Right, absolutely correct. Not only there, not only in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time we will offer 65 ter 173 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit D154, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. D154 is admitted into evidence. And Mr. Kehoe, I'm looking at your last question. You had to have the permission of the army is similarly not distinguishing between factual permission without which you would be obstructed in your movements and whether it was legally right to ask for permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, then I'll clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same problem. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Ermolaev, in order to go into the Cetina valley in July of 1995, you had to go down to the ARSK headquarters in Knin and ask them whether or not an UNMO team could go to that area, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could object. The document states that "UNMO teams should have freedom of movement in the ACR of 1 Brigade North Dalmatian Corps, but to secure their safety there must be permission." It appears from the reading that they can go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems, Mr. Russo, that you're now interpreting the text, which is not appropriate at this time. Where you say that you had to go down to the -- to ask for permission, was that in accordance with the agreed -- I'm not fully aware yet on the basis of what agreement exactly you were operating there, but under the terms of your mandate, were you under an obligation to ask for permission to the ARSK forces or the republican government to seek permission before you could enter a certain area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to the mandate in Sector South UNMOs were supposed to get full freedom of movement in carrying out their obligations, and they were not supposed to get any permission from any authority on this side as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Despite that mandate, in fact you were asking for permission, or the forces insisted on you getting permission before you entered a certain area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. It's a good question. That was the process. A little bit complicated. So from both sides. So from one side we in any case, I mean, teams tried to carry out in spite of all barriers, you know, we experienced in this territory to be able to monitor a situation particularly in Cetina. Sometimes our teams managed to come through and be non-stopped. Sometimes not. And -- but in July and with every passing day you're absolutely correct. We had extremely strict freedom of movement, and in some cases you're absolutely correct. When they went on the 31st, we were allowed to go only with their liaison officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you say we had extremely --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- strict freedom of movement, did you mean to say that your freedom of movement was restricted, or because strict freedom of movement means for me full freedom of movement. But if you say restricted then is it that you were not --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean severely restricted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Restricted. Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just going back to the Cetina valley, there was a restriction on movements by the UNMOs into the Cetina valley in July 1995; correct.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, one of the issues was the shelling during harvesting time, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And General Gotovina -- well, let me just put this on the screen 65 ter 2007. Excuse me, 2079. Thank you very much. I was just corrected in my numbering. We can take a look at this, Mr. Ermolaev. This is an order from General Gotovina dated -- and the date it is sent and received -- or received is 7/16/95 in the lower left-hand corner. And it notes, the subject is suspension of action: "Further to the request of the commander of the south commander and with regard to the suspension of fire action in the area of Cetina ... due to harvesting of the local Serbian population who are carrying out works under the escort of UNCRO patrols, I hereby order: "Suspend the fire actions in the mentioned area of Cetina to a maximum degree therewith enabling harvesting. "In view of the fact that on Wednesday, 19th July ... a meeting with the commander of --" should be Sector South, Jug being Sector South --

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jug Sector South.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- Jug as Sector South. I know. "... has been organised, the details of the request will be separately discussed and a final decision given of which you will be informed." Now, Mr. Ermolaev, were you aware that --

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of this order?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You were never told of this order?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mean, it was not addressed to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No. I'm just -- did you learn about the fact that General Gotovina had --

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. I'm -- I just hear for the first time and I'm really surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour at this time we'll offer 65 ter 200079 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit D155.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D155 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mean General let me bring up a document which is 65 ter 4490. And, Mr. Ermolaev, this is a document that comes from General Gotovina entitled "Supplementary Report on Positions and Types of Enemy Weapons in the Area of Separation," and it -- if we can go to the bottom of page 2, we note at the bottom at number 31, 32 there are some pieces in the village of Cetina and the hamlet of -- excuse me, in Cetina. If we go to the following page I believe it reads -- Palacevici is the hamlet. During the course of your work as an UNMO and as the deputy senior military observer. Were you made aware by the sight of the quantity of the artillery pieces that they had in and about the zone of separation and exactly what those pieces were?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the zone of separations --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may sir, in and around the zone of separation. I don't want to restrict you to just the zone of separation because I know that there were people --

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] yeah. I was there myself and saw Croatians so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are speaking the same language.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you make a pause between question and answer then again between question and answer. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Apologies to the booth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Just turning back, yes. We had information which we were supposed to check, and -- but I cannot and would like to draw attention to have such exact data as General Gotovina had, I can assure you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, at this time we'd like to offer 65 ter 4490 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit D156.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D156 is admitted into evidence. Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in fact -- let me put on the screen 65 ter 2424. We can just -- just blow-up the top part of that, Madam Registrar. The date being 20 July, 1995. And it discusses a meeting with -- in paragraph one between General Gotovina and General Forand. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zadar 20th, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we can just go to the next page, the centre of that page where -- and it begins: "Within the course of further negotiations." Can you just blow that up just a little bit more? That's it. Okay. Good. It notes: "In the course of further negotiations that was based on the central points of the letter by the UNCRO delivered to the commander of ZV Split General Gotovina responded. As for the area of Cetina temporarily occupied area of the RH Republic of Croatia," and by the way, this is a document from the ministry from the Republic of Croatia, "where UNCRO requested from the Croatian side not to shell this area giving as the explanation the fact that local population is engaged in the process of harvesting. Gotovina responded that UNCRO needed to control the fire and positions where Croatian units were being targeted from, and then the civilians would be able to carry out the harvest without hindrance. Otherwise, Croatian artillery would be forced to act in response." Now, Mr. Ermolaev, did UNCRO either under -- the troops under General Forand's commands or the UNMOs under Colonel Hjertnes' and your command, did they take upon the task of controlling these firing -- these Serb firing positions in the Cetina valley?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I stated before, so we didn't know, I mean, exact, I mean, position, and UNMOs were not deployed at the positions where allegedly RSK pieces were deployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, who in the United Nations took it upon themselves to control these firing positions, or did they?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, just to put it bluntly, I -- I just was not so much aware of -- at that particular, you know, days in July about such outcomes. What I do remember, that there -- there was big, you know, discussions about what should be done just with this harvesting time and people living there. That what I clearly remember. And, as well, I clearly remember that I -- I never heard that UNMOs were asked or tasked by General Forand to ensure that there is no firing from these villages. I do not remember, I mean, the consequences and outcomes of his meeting with Gotovina. It's -- and I'm not quite sure whether we have such report from SMO in these days. I'm not quite sure. So -- I only remember that we were pleased when finally it come down there. Just general feelings I remember. But about such taskings and requests from Mr. Gotovina I do not remember absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I take it when you say that you "remember that we were pleased," are you saying that you were pleased that the shelling stopped --

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- so the Serbs could harvest?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for sure. Because we had confirmation from UNMOs. I don't remember the dates, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand. I didn't mean to cut you off. Mr. Ermolaev, I didn't mean to cut you off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please finish your sentence. You said, "Because we had confirmation from UNMOs," you didn't remember the exact date, about what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I -- I do not remember, I mean, the dates when intensive firing reports from this area stopped, and I started getting information that the situation there particularly stabilised. I do not remember exactly days and how long such, you know, peaceful time took place there. But there was a period when I want to confirm that we received no reports from UNMOs about fire reps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would like to offer into evidence 65 ter 2424.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D157.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D157 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. And I'd like to now shift myself a little bit further north and just a few days later, Mr. Ermolaev, and to the area of Strmica, and if I may, I would like to put on the screen 1D100538. Sir, I'd like you to take a look at this map, and we're talking about the time, this was August 1, 1995, with the confrontation line again between the ARSK/ARS being the army of the Republika Srpska, which would be to the north. ARSK is the Republic of Serb Krajina is a little next to that, and the HV/HVO units being on the blue side. Can you take a look at this and you recognise generally this area, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Objection against the question or --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No. I'd like to ask what the provenance of this document is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not objecting, but you're trying to explore who created. Could you inform us, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The people who were involved in the military side of this planning on the HV side had these, and we'll show you many of them as we go through the course of this trial. Frankly, Your Honour, the confrontation lines and the units that are in these areas I didn't think was a subject of dispute, but that being said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're not yet there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are these contemporaneous documents or were they --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Contemporaneous documents. That means that this one, for example, is created on or around the 1st of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, it is. And if I may say this, Judge, contemporaneous, the confrontation lines changed and they what they did is they changed it along. And what I'm -- in this particular instance, this is a smaller recitation of a much larger map, because the confrontation line, of course, extends dramatically far to the south and other areas, and I just wanted to focus on the Strmica area because that is the subject of some issues in the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it has been -- is it -- you said contemporaneous document. You explained to us that it was part of a larger map or set of maps. Now, has it been redacted in any way since then or has it been worked --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I could certainly tell you, Judge, that things like the -- something like the Strmica village down there of course for certain -- first of all, anything that was in there was initially in Croatian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so as we see it now it's not a contemporaneous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's exactly right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a further development of what you say was a map which was created in approximately August 1995. I take it that the agenda, et cetera, also added or are they not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, Judge. The information that's at the top, this is all created by our trial team. Where it says the Strmica village, the English aspects that are in the lower left-hand corner, the situation Grahavo-Strmica, 01 August 1995, those types of issues were reference issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, are the originals still available? I mean it might be very practical the way of presenting these maps with English text of course has major advantages. And nevertheless, I can imagine that Mr. Russo is more concerned about whether it reflects what originally was in these maps. Mr. Russo, is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there anyway to figure out on the basis of the originals that Mr. Russo can see how skillfully your team translated the original information in such a way that the Chamber can easily understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The answer to that is yes, Judge. There are -- if I can clarify this. There are -- as we move from winter 1994 to various stages of this, jump one, jump two summer 1995, you will see the confrontation lines move. This was attempted to be a snapshot of a particular time in this is August 1, late July or early August of 1995, and it's taken from that; but if the counsel wants to see the underlying data, hard data from which this was taken from, we'll gladly produce it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking this because you said there was still a lot to come. So therefore in order to avoid further discussions about it, Mr. Russo, this offer, this spontaneous offer by Mr. Kehoe, is that -- does that satisfy you? Of course, if Mr. Russo would find out later that the information is distorted, distorted and not accurate, then, of course, I take it that you would have no problem that he revisits the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Absolutely not, Judge. I -- I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Under those circumstances, Mr. -- are you sufficiently informed, Mr. Russo, about the source of this map, and are you satisfied that with this opportunity to verify that if Mr. Kehoe is tendering it that there will be no objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now -- thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ermolaev, in late July, early August of 1995, there was activity up in the Strmica area, was there not?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And Strmica was an area where the ARSK had a lot of personnel and equipment, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Strmica area was monitored by UN battalions, so I -- I just can only reference to the information battalions had at the time. So I have no information about in the area because it was not the zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, if I -- if I may, sir, you did consult with the UN battalions, and that would be the Kenyan Battalion? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let -- let me explain and return back again. So I mean we did not consult anyone, because I mean the structure of UNMOs is an independent institution as well as battalions. We carry out, I mean, every day cooperation, but usually if the area -- usually battalions are to be deployed along confrontation lines or zone of separation so that's everywhere and -- so if as a rule such a hot-spot, I mean, confrontation line, zone of separation, as a rule we deploy there stationary battalions observation post. And we did not see a necessity to deploy close to UN battalion posts as well UNMOs, because we didn't have too many UNMOs for the whole sector. I had 80 persons and General Forand had 13.000, so you can imagine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand. But going back to my initial question, Mr. Ermolaev, the Kenyan Battalion was the battalion that was located in and around Strmica in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, there was -- was there or was there not to your knowledge a significant ARSK position in Strmica in late July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would answer in another question. I was fully aware that there was some combat activities between conflicting sides in that direction, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time before I move off this map I would like to tender this map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Subject to the caveats that we discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D158.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I come back to your last answer, Mr. Ermolaev. You were asked whether to your knowledge there was a significant ARSK position in Strmica in late July of 1995. Then you said you would answer in another question, although no question then followed, because you said, "I was fully aware that there was some combat activities between the conflicting sides." Why not just answer the question whether you were aware of a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of positions of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- of conflicting sides, weaponry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't know now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I don't know I just say no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let me address ourselves to 65 ter 1344. Thank you very much. Mr. Ermolaev, this is an order that comes from the 7 corps command, the ARSK notes -- order on sending units to any tank detachment. To the command of the 7 mixed anti-tank artillery regiment and the 2nd Infantry Brigade. Urgent. "Under the current circumstances and with the aim of preventing further advance of Ustasha in the direction of Grahovo-Strmica, I hereby issue the following: "Order. "Send 100 millimetre T-anti-tank guns from the 7th mixed anti-tank artillery regiment to Tactical Group 2. "Send 9K11 anti-armour missile systems platoon from 2nd Infantry Brigade to Tactical Group 2. "Send units as standard formations with standard issue equipment. "Units carrying pioneer tools with them. "Units must report to Colonel Stevo Draskovic," I think it should be in the area of the Golubic MUP by 1600 hours on 31 July 1995. "Commanders of all units will prepare ... at the Tactical Group to command post in the area of the village of Strmica to the commander of the 7th corps by 1400 hours on 31 July ... "Commanders will prepare units and bring them to the designated areas." Mr. Ermolaev, on this document dated 31 July, did you and your UNMOs observe the ARSK moving personnel and weaponry to the Strmica area?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember such reports from UNMOs, and I do want to say that we had, you know, restrictions of movement as I mentioned before, and we must check the reports. But I do believe they really conducted such a redeployment, I don't think that they allowed us to move out from our place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when it came to going to the Strmica area, there were restrictions of movement on the UNMOs?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll offer 65 ter 1344.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit D159.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. D159 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Kehoe, I don't know whether you're touching upon a new subject or not. The Chamber would like to start a break within the next two to seven minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Judge, we can take a break now. That's fine. I could pick up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will resume at a quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Ermolaev, there is a chance that we might not finish today. Are you still available on Thursday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to return back tomorrow. I have some meetings, appointments already done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there anyway you can, because going and then having to return might be a bit of a problem for you as well. Is there any way that you could reschedule your return?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, to my regret I would not like to. This is really important to me, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's understood that you'd rather not do that. At the same time -- I'll consider it with my colleagues, and I also can imagine that you do not feel free in an open court session to give the reasons why it's so urgent for you to go back, and if there's any other way in which you'd like to inform the Chamber about your personal reasons why it's so important for that you can return tomorrow rather than one day later, then we'll find a way to do that. Because you'll understand that there's also a great interest to hear your testimony and in terms of procedure it's always to be preferred not to interrupt, apart from all the other aspects, that you would have to return, that we have additional costs, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You see that when we discussed the days, windows, as we say, which I could find in my schedule, I applied just for May, but I was asked to find days, this five days, and so I rescheduled everything. And so first of all I had some great issues on a personal events in my family, first of all, and that's why I asked just to postpone it a bit. It's okay with my work. I just rescheduled it. So I had two important -- three important events on 26th, 29th. My wife and my mother's birthdays. Today is my mother's birthday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Congratulation to start.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. And then I promised my daughter the final, I mean important event, in my life, so is one year celebration of her marriage, and I promised to her that in any case I will be there, and then I rescheduled my studies with my students starting from the 2nd May. So it's a bit problematic to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the celebration of this one year would be --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 1st May, right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1st of May. That would then be on Thursday. Morning, afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Departure, morning, afternoon so I have tickets reserved for at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand, but celebration on the 1st of May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 1st of the May, right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The whole of the day or? I'm not trying to find out about your family, perhaps even secret arrangements.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At least we agree that afternoon, so for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just raising one matter that I imagine the Court has considered, but I would have felt bad if not mentioning is the possibility of extending into the afternoon in light of the current competing court schedules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There might be an opportunity for that, but I have to attend an initial appearance early in after the noon, which, however, keeps me not busy for more than 45 minutes to one hour, and I'd like to ask Madam Registrar to find out whether ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ermolaev we're doing our utmost best. Madam Registrar will further inquire into the possibilities of continuing to sit this afternoon although that would not be immediately at 2.15 but perhaps at 3.00 or 4.00. If that is for Defence counsel, I'm just inquiring whether that would be a possibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed, Mr. Kehoe. Yes. I asked the presence of Mr. Ermolaev because the Chamber had in mind to -- and of course we -- to grant another hour after this morning's session, which will finish at 1.45. Of course the Chamber had in mind that Witness 69 will not testify this week, so therefore we might have a little bit more time than we initially scheduled. We'll hear from the registrar. Of course, Mr. Kehoe, it's a bit of a problem now because we don't know where we're heading. Focus at the most important things first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I could just bring up 65 ter 1346.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Ermolaev, this is order that is ordering the formation -- it comes from the army of the Republika Srpska Krajina, an order to form a units of 80 men who will be engaged in a combat task in the village of Strmica. I take it from your prior answers that you were unaware of these types of troop gatherings; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll offer 65 ter 1346 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit D160.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D160 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We can turn our attention to 65 ter 194. And again this is a document coming from the Republic of Serb --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm getting a little ahead of myself, Judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is a diary from -- provided by the Office of the Prosecutor. The assistant commander for logistics. If we can go to page 3 in the -- I'm sorry. I've been reminded he's commander of the logistics for the ARSK. If we turn to page 3 and scroll up just a bit, we can just look at the inclusions of --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Go you can scroll that up just a bit, Madam Registrar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Inclusion of ammunition being sent up to the Strmica area. I take it, sir, you were unaware of this -- this as well given your other answers about movement of ammunition by the RSK to Strmica?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I -- I do not know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if you see down there on the 7th of July -- excuse me, the 31st of July, 1995, it notes: "I was informed that ammunition was loaded onto 12 railroad shippers in order to remove the Golubic," should be "to remove the Golubic depot," should be "to the Golubic depot." Sir, were you aware that they were using their rail lines to move ammunition?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I not remember such a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour at this time I would move 65 ter 194 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honours, is he moving in the entire diary or just the portion?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I am moving in pages 1 through 10, which is the part that has been translated by the -- by the Language Services.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit D161.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D161 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might have just one moment, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me put up 1D100539, and this is a -- I have distributed paper copies on this, Your Honour, and I've just translated one excerpt from this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, you are so kind to correct an apparently wrong translation although it's from handwriting, so it could also how to decipher that portion. It says that the translation is unrevised. I think especially since you are --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- already correcting that the translation should be a final one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: By the way, we don't need to go back to this. In the insert of the prior document, which would be D161, if we look at the bottom of that you see that, sir? At the bottom two lines it says "At 1800 I had ordered the transfer of 12 shippers loaded with ammunition to tunnels." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: "To tunnels," yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you aware during the period of time you were there that they were moving their ammunition on railway lines through the tunnel system that was in Sector South? Are you still thinking, sir? I don't mean to move you --

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm just trying to remember generally. 31st, 1600 -- well, it's a bit difficult. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I mean, let's talk about the area -- the period of time when the ARSK was operating in Sector South in your AOR, area of responsibility. Did you see them moving ammunition on the rail lines?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that, yes, we had reports from different movements of military, but I do not remember exact dates and teams reporting, but we clearly observed a repositioning of RSK in most cases, but in such particular case, 31st July, 1600, I just do not remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I -- I fully confirm that they were -- in spite of our, you know, restrictions of movement, when we succeeded we saw such redeployments of military, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can go to 1D100539.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I can't say that it's completely clear to me yet. To remove to the Golubic depot and then a couple of lines later it goes to tunnels. Is the Golubic depot in tunnels, or is it -- how do we -- that -- I just put to you that it's not clear whether these are the same 12 railroad shippers. The number at least is the same. I'm not asking you to give evidence, but at least inform you that this creates some confusion as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, what -- and we can work on the translation, but my understanding coming from the B/C/S is that they were going to the Golubic depot and using this -- these railway cars to take ammunition out. We can work on this translation further, but it's taken from a written diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for this moment for you to know that it confuses a bit. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Madam Registrar, if --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I do believe we, Mr. Ermolaev, we did give you a paper copy of this particular exhibit which is an excerpt of (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: (redacted). Now, this is dated the 30th of July, 1995. Now, you sent Mr. Tchernetsky up to Strmica in and about that time, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that was before 1400, because what I remember, he departed Sector South HQ, then they were supposed to pick up liaison officer, who was supposed just to give them a movement there. So I think that was in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And when you sent him up there he was being escorted by ARSK --

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I think so he -- he was escorted. Right. So it's okay. Good.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did he report back to you the units or any such as what we have in this particular document that was described by this ARSK soldier? Did he report back seeing anything like this? And this, I'm referring to the document that's before you.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the one I see on the screen on the 30th July?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, the 30th of July, sir. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I'll offer 1D100539 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit D162.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D162 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, there ended up being in the latter part of July and early August quite a bit of shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Could we move into a private session for a minute?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes we'll move into a private session. I'm not yet aware for what reason, but I take it that you have a serious reason, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Ermolaev, let me turn your attention to 65 ter 1353. This is the cover sheet of an UNCRO report dated 31 July 1995. If we can go to page 2. And towards the bottom of the page there is the excerpt D, "Sector South." And it reads: "The situation in the sector remains tense, especially in the south-east corner of the sector where 115 artillery shells were fired or impacted (30 HV and 88 RSK). Now, the south-east corner of the sector is the area that's covered by CanBat, isn't?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the area referring to this shelling that's reported on 31 July 1995, is the shelling that's taking place from and into Strmica, isn't it? Well, let's read the rest of it?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "Higher than normal level of air activities in the northern part of the sector. Could not be assessed whether it's linked in activities in the Bihac pocket of Bosanski or B. Grahovo. The ARSK are reacting to events in Bosanski -- or B. Grahovo by redeploying forces. However, the HV so far does not appear to close with or cross the border. The sector assessed the Croatian efforts in the face of ARSK opposition as 'unlikely' in the Dinara area. The situation at Strmica is being monitored closely to foresee the situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina which might spill over into the sector and to make sure the security of UN troops." Now, based on your recollection and also you can refer to your statement of P94 at page 4, the shelling that was taking place there was shelling in and around Strmica, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And at this particular point the assessment that you recall from UNCRO is that the HV was not going to be successful in defeating the ARSK.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who said this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Or did they. I mean, I'm just saying this because it says here --

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- if you read this "The sector assessed the Croatian forces in the face of ARSK opposition as unlikely in the Dinara area." Do you take that to mean that the assessment is that if the HV attacks they will be unsuccessful?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would not like to comment the conclusions of battalions, but I didn't have such feelings at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time we will offer 65 ter 1353 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D163.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D163 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge, I think I just threw away my number to this document -- this document. If I might have a moment. It is 65 ter 3122.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is another -- the cover sheet is dated 2 August 1995. The date becomes significant because there is a -- if we can turn to page 2 and the general situation, it notes that: "The situation in Sector South was in recent days calm and stable. Exchanges of indirect fire continue in the Strmica area. The RSK has moved its guns eastward and the exchanges are more even, even than they have been. Indications of moderate to heavy fighting in the bordering areas of Bosnia-Herzegovina are heard, including air activity originating in the RSK." And if we can scroll down that page, we note from the warring party activity at -- on the 2nd of August -- we'll just take a look at it this. I mean it says 2nd of August, but if I might just one moment scroll up to the top of that page so I can correct something. If we can scroll up. This document notes that it's April, but the body says August, does it not sir?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it's April on it, [indiscernible] to April 27th, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But it's -- the body at the bottom is talking about August 1995. If we can go back to the warring party activity. If we can blow-up that number 3. In those three points in August on the 2nd, it notes the exchange of gunfire between -- excuse me, artillery fire between HV/HVO, as well as the ARSK, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So bit --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour at this time I'll offer 65 ter 3122 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit D164.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D164 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, Mr. Ermolaev, the latter part of July and the first few days of August there is a significant amount of fighting going on up in the Strmica area, at least shell-fire in the Strmica area between the HV and the ARSK, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us talk a little bit about -- I'm going to shift subjects here and I want to talk a little bit about the shelling of Knin. And I want to ask you a couple of questions, at least initially. You note in your statement, and I am talking about P94 -- I'm sorry. P95, paragraph 11. You note that: "I do not believe that the shelling of Knin on 4-5 August was intended to destroy military targets, because the RSK Ministry of Defence building was neither destroyed nor seriously damaged." Do you see that hard copy, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: What page number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is page 7 of your 2007 statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Page 7, it should be paragraph 11.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, you said that in your statement. Is it your testimony before this Trial Chamber that the only military target in Knin was the RSK Ministry Of Defence?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think it's a bit out of the context that we discussed with the Prosecutor. So I was asked a question about provisional assessment of -- of Colonel Steinar that the shellings these days bore exclusively military out of the 70 they found, and we discussed already this document and my assessment, so I -- I do believe that it's a little bit, you know, misunderstanding here, and that was to some extent, I mean, an answer that the only targets on the 4th and 5th were exclusively civilians. Just to correct a bit, what I meant to say, that -- that I do not believe that the shelling of Knin on the 4th and 5th of August was intended to destroy exclusively military targets. Let me say so, because for sure, I mean, there were military targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, there were in fact military targets near where you lived, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now let us bring up a map which has been previously received in evidence as Exhibit P78. Now, if I could use that, and if we could go to the area that is marked with a C and blow-up that area. That's in the left-hand side. Do you see that there? Okay. And just scroll down a little bit. Now, sir, you see that letter C in the centre of that page?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, where you lived was just a little bit down from that, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And how far did you live away from the North Dalmatian Corps barracks? Approximately.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, everything is very -- very close in Knin, you know, and so it's a little bit difficult, but, well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it not more than 50 to a hundred metres, or was it by far more.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think a bit more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us how much?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I can't be so much exact, you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- with the metres, maybe you can get some information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, isn't it true that we have the marking on the map where the witness lived and that we have clear map where we are aware of the northern barracks, where that is, clearly defined areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We can measure it, Judge. I mean, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the area that is designated as C, a Prosecution witness testified, and this is Andreis Dreyer, Page 1720, to, if I may, line 25 going over to page 1721 lines 1 and 4, and you see the C at that location and he's talking about the 4th of August. If we could look at that marking, C, which the registrar is ahead of me and doing very well, "Is it correct that this is a mortar section you observed by the school?" Answer "Yes?" Now, on the morning of the 4th did you see a mortar section at that location marked with C?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, that location, sir, was - again without specific distances - relatively close to your residence, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Absolutely I cannot confirm whether there was something or not, because, you know, we spent time in the basement and then we just departed with APC. I didn't have time just to have a look. We were running into APC, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, when you were in the basement did you hear any type of weapon being fired from that location?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, I -- I can assure you that it's impossible being in the basement when there is conducted alongside at the same time with the same, I mean, targeting different kinds of usage of weaponry, just to peek out one weaponry which maybe even standing close to you. No. I couldn't -- let me put it in such a way: I couldn't even theoretically identify, I mean, any outgoing, which at least as I understood from your statement or from statement of this person. No. I cannot confirm it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So basically you couldn't confirm either ingoing or outgoing shell-fire, as to who was responsible, could you?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you noted in your statement that -- and this is your statement of P94, and it's page 4, last paragraph. If you can take a look at it for yourself, sir. I mean, I just -- I don't want to read it and not give you the opportunity to look at it. You have that, sir, page 4?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you note on the bottom of the page: "Speaking of destruction in Knin residential areas as a result of shelling, I would like to --" and I'm sure you said make two points, but it says "to -- two points. First the Croatian army conducted an unprecedented massive artillery rocket launcher mortar fire against Knin and surrounding areas where there were tens of thousands of civilians. I spent eight months in Bosnia, in Tuzla, and Sarajevo, and such unproportioned destruction, use of fire against civilians I've never seen." Now -- now, sir, you also noted in your statement of - this is P95 - at page -- P95, paragraph 10, page 7, the second to last sentence, when asked to comment on this -- do you have that paragraph 10? And you note that: "I was in my office for most of the day during the 4th and the 5th and was not actively observing the shelling." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when you made this statement in -- back in 1997 and signed in 2002 about this unprecedented destruction, you hadn't even observed the shell-fire, had you?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, first of all I -- I observed the shell-fire. There's no doubt about it. And secondly, yeah, I answered the question. Yes, I observed it myself as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it is clearly stated here. I was in my office most of the day and was not actively observing the shelling. It clearly stated here that I was not standing and 24 hours observing shelling of Knin, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So -- I'm sorry. So let --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, Judge? No? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you made that statement in your statement -- you made that comment in your statement of, if I may, of P94 where you spent most of the day in your office; right?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let's turn our attention to, if I may, before we even get to that particular sitrep -- let us put P83 on the screen. Now, this note, sir, this is the letter that was sent by General Forand, and it notes in the first sentence or sent by General or drafted by General Forand or signed by him. "So this was a protest in the most vigorous manner, the unprovoked artillery attack on Knin and the towns of Drnis, Medak, Bunic, Benkovac, and Kistanje." Now, Mr. Ermolaev, did you have anything to do with the writing of this letter or the selecting of these particular towns when they were put in this letter?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is the time of this protest, do we know?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, that's a very good question, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's a fair chance that it would be the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, no. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: He's talking about temporally, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I think he's talking about within the 24-hour time frame.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, in this letter I didn't participate in issuing this protest. So that was done by General Forand without consulting me. So he did it as usual way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you had nothing to do with this list of these towns?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now let us turn our attention to D -- I don't know if I have this date correct. I believe it's D5, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I guess that's always a good start. It is D5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in D5, if we -- this is a sitrep from 1610 on the -- 1610 in the afternoon on the 4th of August, 1995. I direct your attention to paragraph 4. By the way -- by the way, Mr. Ermolaev, did you write this?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the style would be different from mine. So I mean, it's -- I think released yes, but [indiscernible] yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you approved the content?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: All right. Let's talk about paragraph 4. "The initial shelling of the centre of Knin was coordinated with artillery attacks -- with artillery attack along the ZOS, zone of separation. Other civilian centres of Krajina were indiscriminately targeted." Now, you approved that what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, what centres, civilian centres, were indiscriminately targeted?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we just have a look further on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sure. Absolutely. You can take --

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: UNMOs reported and we can should find the answer this -- or further reports about it. Let's have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can just take that back to normal size so the witness can look at the document. Maybe take it up a little bit. Thank you. And there is another page. And, Mr. Ermolaev, if you tell me when you're ready to go to the next page. I don't want to rush you, but there is page 2 at some point.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it. "Incoming mortar fire had been within 100 metres of UNMOs teams." Yes. I'm finished this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And could we go to the next page, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And can we return back, please, to the first page?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Absolutely. Absolutely. Mr. Ermolaev, if you want any portion of that blown up yet further. I know sometimes it's difficult to hear [sic]. I certainly have some difficulty with it, so please ask and I'm sure the registrar can do that for us.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: And can we see the times and the purpose this --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Absolutely, sir. Can you see that? Do you want it blown up a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We're talking about the top of the page, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So that must be the report for -- for 4 hours. And do we have the report for -- so it's 16 -- 1600, right? Okay. Good. So I just looked through, yes. I'm ready to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is there any reporting that you see in here from any of the UNMO teams that note that civilian centres were indiscriminately targeted?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Okay. Thank you. So the first -- during the beginning of reporting of the situation in the Sector South, you know, immediately we tried to redeploy UNMOs from their locations. You can see from their reports that they were being shelled 5.100 metres from their positions. And I received the reports about general situation in the sector from General Forand office and operations officer from battalion's headquarters. So that's why initially, initially, the information received there about the results, what was seen and heard by 13.000 UN soldiers in the sector, they were giving only highlights about general assessment. Later on we decided just that such a report must include battalions' assessments and what they see on the ground. So that's why later I discussed it with Sector South, UN battalion sector, and we -- and we started including, and we already run through that report from some date, I do not remember the timings, started including such reports on the basis of which, I mean, highlights and general assessment had been done. So generally, I mean, the sense, the feelings that was reported here we can see give the same assessment as was given by General Forand. And to this extent we closely cooperated and discussed the situation, and if battalions it is reliable United Nations information source for us so that's why we cannot say that everything is calmed down when battalions reports our situation across the sector. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you -- so you're saying that this particular comment is based on observations by UNCRO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So -- and based on the observations, did you write down someplace for the benefit of the UNMO headquarters in Zagreb what you were being told about indiscriminate fire on individual villages? Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Well, good question. Yes. So first of all I do want to understand the jury [phoen], and because we all the time just returning back to the same question. So we must clearly understand that UNMOs, it was little bit not fully fledged, you know, I mean, military organisation. It included only several, you know, UNMOs on the spot. So that's why we for sure used the materials from UN battalions and assessments done by the sector commander. Secondly, about assessments which were given in the first hours when they were started. We must clearly understand that UNMOs, as well as battalions, worked in real combat situations. It is very good to sit here and, you know, just discuss what I was writing during the wartime. For sure, I mean, later on we started improving, and we felt it as well. So that's why we included not only general assessment that battalions gave us but as well if they saw it included that. But we tried to divide information which was received by UNMOs, and we clearly see it, that here we included the highlights, the protest letter we see which confirmed the situation on the ground there. So the war started. What do you -- how do you expect it to be reported. And here we see that destruction started across Knin and in other cities reported by battalions and et cetera. I mean, on commanding level we give general assessment, and for sure later on such mechanism of reporting so to maximum extent to which battalions or UNMOs could do it they did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when you got -- let's go back to P83 again then. So when you got this information from the UNCRO battalions, I assume that you got the information about the individual towns of -- that are listed in this letter in addition to Knin. And I'm talking about Drnis, Medak, Bunic, Benkovac, and Kistanje; right?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now after you got that information, after Operation Storm, and in this letter it says an artillery attack on these places, did you go -- did the UNMOs good back to those villages and do an artillery assessment on the artillery fire on each of those villages? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, if you put a composite question to the witness you can't ask him to say yes or no. It could be that they went back but did not do an artillery -- whatever. But if you want a yes or no, then the question should be --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'll ask a general question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did --

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I'm answer. I got your point. No doubt about it. It's not a problem. I will answer it. You know, after Operation Storm, okay, I do understand that you mean in general, in September or October, whatever. I mean, situation on the ground allowed. Am I correct in understanding you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You are correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. At least not there in these days. So I never received from United Nations Zagreb any instructions to change the mission of UNMOs and start conducting a greater analysis of the Operation Storms and et cetera. We had clear mandate to monitor situation on the ground with the -- that we discussed already, and I didn't get such orders to investigate and conduct greater analysis. As well to the best of my knowledge, battalions' engineers, they as well didn't do, but it's better to clarify with them. I never received such new additional taskings to my ten persons or whatever. I mean, you know, I was very much limited with -- very limited with my resources just to provide, you know, PRAC [phoen] activities, to provide civil affairs, to provide you know this one and just having at your disposal several tens of brave, you know, international community representatives. No. For sure not. Could I not even imagine such a taskings to UNMOs to conduct, you know, a greater analysis in August, September, while the situation on the ground and decision of the United Nations was to monitor the situation. I'm sorry, we didn't do it. I never received any order from my direct command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, it's a quarter to 2.00. There's an option to continue this hearing this afternoon in courtroom 2 immediately after the initial appearance which will take place in courtroom 1, this disadvantage being that your whole teams might not fit into the courtroom. Another option would be to continue in this courtroom but then we need to have an hour break. Now, my estimate is that the initial appearance will not take more than 45 minutes up to one hour, although you never know in advance. That would mean in this courtroom we most likely would be able to continue at a quarter to 4.00, whereas in the other courtroom we might be able to continue at quarter past 3.00 approximately. That's one. Second, if we sit is this afternoon, time would be limited to one session, that is, at the most one hour and 45 minutes. As I said before, Mr. Kehoe, you would have another hour so that 45 minutes remain for other questions. Of course I do not know whether there needs further redistribution of the time available to the Defence among the teams. I take it that the other teams would -- Mr. Cayley, I'm looking at you. You're not putting huge claims on --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It depends what arises, as always, but I anticipate nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Same here, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Kehoe, you have one hour available. We will then adjourn and we'd like to see you back, Mr. Ermolaev. We all know that family life is a fundamental right, although not under all circumstances.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Even in the Russian Federation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From what I understand the Russian Federation is a party to the European Convention on Human Rights as is many other countries. We will resume in this case half an hour after the initial appearance has finished, which starts at a quarter past 2.00 in this courtroom this afternoon.
