utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Madam Registrar, I never know whether such a continuation is the continuation of the morning session or just a new session. Just out of an abundance of caution would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kehoe, I'm looking at the clock. We're now at 3.28. I'll give you until 4.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I feel privileged, Judge. Sixty-two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Ermolaev, I'd just ask us to look at the screen. It's the document that we looked at previously, P83, that notes town of Bunic. Do you see that? The village of Bunic, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn our attention to P100, the document my colleague Mr. Kuzmanovic talked to you about this morning. And I want to turn your -- just if you could look at P100 first, the face page. If you could just blow that up a little bit. Yes. Thank you. It's an UNMO report of 4 August at 1040. And if we can turn to the second page. And towards the top of that page we see the -- in the right above the CanBat AOR: "OPSZC 31, Bunic.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: CanBat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, above CanBat.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Actually the paragraph above CanBat that begins "OPSCZ 31 Bunic"?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "Bunic is in critical condition. ARSK suffered large casualties, Bunic and Colonel Savo ordered to take transport means from this OP. CzechBat soldiers did not want to issue them and ARSK started shooting. Then CzechBat persons in this OP issued," and it says, "1 APC and terrain --" although I'm not sure exactly what that is, "car." Now, Bunic, sir, was a brigade headquarters for the ARSK, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I do not remember each brigade headquarters and I cannot comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with Colonel Savo, the Krajina Serb colonel who's mentioned in this sitrep? Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us move ahead. And I want to talk to you about another sitrep, 124. That would be D125. Excuse me. Now, if we can look at the -- just wait for the ELMO to load. This is a sitrep of 5 August 1995, and in the highlights it says: "Two Czech soldiers died while awaiting Croatian authorisation for evacuation." Did you write that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Let us churn to the CzechBat reporting section, and I ask you -- and that's on the next page. And please look at the section under "Military information," and what CzechBat reported in their AOR. Now, there is nothing in that report that reflects your assessment that Czech soldiers died while awaiting Croatian authorisation for evacuation, is there?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. About this episode, I'd like to inform that actually, I mean, United Nations UNMO teams, and I do believe at that it must be here in daily sitreps, so practically, you know, soldiers from this particular area, when they were living there, OPs, they came to our location, United Nations UNMOs, and initially, if I remember correctly, so gradually, I mean, our UN UNMOs house, there was several, you know, Czech soldiers. They came to us there more and more initially. And that's why all information regarding their transportation, the status of soldiers, their injuries, and et cetera, et cetera, that was conducted and observed physically by UNMOs on the spot, and we received this information, particularly from UNMOs of this team who give their place for these soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My question to you, sir, there is nothing in what they reported that reflects that Czech soldiers died while awaiting Croatian authorisation for evacuation, is there?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ermolaev, if the question is whether there's anything in that report, then I think you could say yes or no. And if Mr. Kehoe is seeking new explanation for the situation, or if you would like to add that, please first answer the question and then we'll see what else we would hear from you. Apart from that, Mr. Kehoe, D125, is for me a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I thought you were correcting yourself. At least on the transcript it reads sitrep D124, that is D125, but I now understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just let me read it if I'm correct, just, please, so on the 5th/7/00, two UN soldiers on OPT23 were seriously wounded (died at 1000) and the bodies are still in T23." So we clearly have indicators in this report about status of two UN soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, when the Czech medical people tried to get up there, the report reflects that their APC was taken by the ARSK, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, you know, all details. You're just asking me about why I just put that soldiers two soldiers. We see the report as well as reports of my UNMOs. About APC whether it was taken or not. I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us go to a video and this is an HTV video from 5 August, 1995, 1D100500.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir this, a video of a conversation with the Czech medical personnel from Sector South headquarters. Start from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "Everything happens from this morning "Yeah. We arrived there at half past -- half past 9.00, and then we were -- we were stopped by Serbian side, and they -- so they didn't want to -- to -- to let us through this -- this check-point. They said, 'We have to wait for our commander, our commander.' Their commander wasn't there. So we were -- we were waiting for 20 -- 20 minutes. And then some guys, but not commanders, not their commander, said that we can go there but by foot, not by APC, by our APC. And -- "[Indiscernible]. "Half the guys from Tango 23 will take a middle of the way and we will take another. "Mm-hmm and they will meet [indiscernible]. "That's correct. Right. "So those people who were dead they are -- they were from Tango 23? "I'm sorry? "These dead people they were from -- "From Tango 23, yeah."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now -- now, Mr. Ermolaev, did you discuss what happened at CzechBat with these medical personnel from Sector South headquarters when they returned to Sector South headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I'm not quite sure that they returned to Sector South headquarters and they for sure not. They couldn't have returned because they were from Cern [phoen] battalion. And secondly, well, I answer this question. No, I didn't speak to these people, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the time that they -- on the video that they were stopped was 9.30. Isn't that what he said?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the time in the CzechBat sitrep is 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I'd like to offer the HTV video into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D165.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D165 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, changing subjects one more time and then talking to you about a document that you introduced into evidence, which is P97. If we can bring that up. Now, you recall that, sir, your report?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And in part of that report was -- were the annexes was P98. If we can move to P98.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can we blow that up just a bit, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you see that document well enough, Mr. Ermolaev, to -- to orient yourself with this?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, this -- these -- these numbers in here, where do these numbers come from, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: So these numbers come from the report of UNMOs Sector South.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And who put this together?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this signature here of the officer in charge, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ermolaev, do you know, then please tell us, and do not try to find from signatures who may have --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, but the question is so much general who did it I answered UNMO Sector South. Who just put it together, so my headquarters, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But do you know an individual person who put it together?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you don't remember, just tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. I'm sorry Judge, I didn't mean ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, as part of this document you had another annex which was a summary of human rights violations. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we can pull up P68 so we can orient the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, this -- this, I believe you testified, at least the segment of P68 that goes from 7 August 1995 through 4 September 1995 was, I believe, an annex to your report; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, looking at these sitreps, is the information that is contained in P98, the numbers in P98, is that information that was taken from the situation report extracts that we have in P60 -- P68?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least to the best what I remember, just a bit different, let me say, directions of reporting. So first of all in this summary which is given here, I mean, we mostly included those information, okay, which we received on daily basis from United Nations military observers on the ground. So practically partially this information could be found in daily sitreps. Returning back to the first annex with the number of figures that you asked me, that was a special table developed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ermolaev --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Here again the question was quite simple, whether the numbers, whether the data in this report, whether they are taken from the daily sitreps as Mr. Kehoe said, P60 to P68. What you're now doing you're describing on how these reports were put together, which might be very interesting to know, but is not an answer to the question of Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, okay, if -- well, okay. Well, my answer -- well, to me very clear. Maybe, you know, we have different, you know, methods of thinking. I do understand this. So the reports, the basics for this report, there were special taskings of UNMO to filling such format and they did it. According to the format they received and they informed you that somewhere in the middle of August there was a meeting with the taskings that they should collect such information particular for this table and that's why their information, well, they were collecting, would be different would be from the information which was compiled from daily sitreps. So that was a purposeful task, specific task, which we received and they carried it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But still then you said they were collecting the data. Where did they collect them from? Did they collect them to -- did they take them, extract them from the sitreps, or did they have any other source.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's a clear answer please continue, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wanted to explain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If it didn't come from the sitreps, where did it come from?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: So again we return to the bases, you know, of operations, who is tasking it. So we were staying there before my departure for CTOs, there was conducted a meeting where UNMOs were tasked to start collecting information about each village, each centre, and to check how many people left there, to put it down, and to prepare summary report that we were requested to do, and so such a position, I mean, while they were collecting information by the date they were supposed to present it, so that's why some information according to this format was collected and reported not in realtime, because you know -- I mean, it was difficult. Later on we changed the system. Steinar, he changed a bit, and we -- due to the fact that we did not have sufficient personnel as well as UNCIVPOL, we decided that Knin area and the area around it, all the villages there would be monitored by UN police, because we didn't have too many people, you know, to go everywhere, and everyone was asking, you know, what's going on. So that's why I want to be clear that everything, I mean, was done subsequently the system to ensure that we can cover more and more areas to comply with the decision and orders we received from UN Zagreb. So they were in large adjusted, but for this particular question that you asked me I'm just returning back and want to pinpoint attention to the jury [phoen]. So we had special format worked out together with human rights and civil affairs office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you're saying sir, and correct me if I'm wrong, because I'd like you to be as precise on this as possible, that the collection of a numbers of houses that were burnt, for instance, the collection of that money, that number in P98 did not come from the sitreps?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It did not?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I just said what I'm saying. Partially such information is included in sitrep. That's why you cannot, I mean, find identical figures in that annex and in the annex of particular question how many houses were burnt. I want to draw attention of the jury [phoen]. There are two different absolutely purposes. So the purpose of this one to investigate the number of houses being burned down and how many people live there, because ICRC requested it, because food distribution, water, et cetera. So that was another mission. The second one, annex as you asked me, was particularly to summarise that within these taskings new was reported in daily sitrep that high command just not to open daily sitreps again and do it just to combine it together to make it easier for UN UNMOs headquarters Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, you are aware that in the P68 that's on the screen, and we can page through this, literally every page has insertions in there of number of houses burnt. You know that?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned, you know, practically maximum information that we had regarding new taskings we received was included here because we don't have any other information to be reported.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So the answer to my question is yes, it is, the number of houses that are burnt is included in the situation report that you see before you as P68?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. He's been asked this question now twice --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and we have received unclear answers twice as well. Therefore, let me put it quite simple to you. We have this list with all the numbers in it. Now, you explained to us that those data had been collected at a separate occasion for separate purposes, yes. Now, was the information we find in the sitreps, was that information, as far as burning houses and destruction of houses concerned, was that also considered or was it totally separate and was it total -- totally separate set of data collected? And was that taken into consideration, these sitrep reports about houses burned and destroyed, or was it just a totally separate collection of data?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So summary of humanitarian violations, okay, from my headquarters. So it was primarily based on daily sitreps of UNMOs from the teams as well as daily sitreps of these headquarters to Zagreb regarding to humanitarian violations. If we see the previous table, so, for example, we have a village which was reported, for example, 20 burning house, they saw, for example, today, it doesn't mean that after they were tasking that such a number was the final one and, for example, they go to this place and the number of people living there, so -- and when they go this message so alongside -- I -- I just repeat again that information is included, what they reported yesterday, but as well there was some additional pinpoint if they needed, if they didn't find or didn't -- there was not sufficient enough or just re-check it, so they did it separately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ermolaev, it's still it's rather unclear to me. What I want to know, and it's really a very simple question, were these sitreps among the sources which assisted in compiling that list of violations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were there other sources apart from the sitreps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The sources only additional data received subsequently by UNMOs regarding this or that objective.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There were other sources. Now, please proceed Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But I mean only UNMOs. Not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What you tell us that the additional sources were still UNMOs or also --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- although not contained in the sitreps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And what forms did those other sources take? The information source, what other information source did they take -- what form did they take, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: So during this meeting, and on 14th, 15th, before my departure in any case, all UNMOs including those deployed in Croatian side, right? So Steinar put in new order. So -- and for the first time we had UNMOs deployed on that side of former zone of separation. They started participate -- so we redeployed all our forces just to be able to monitor the whole areas. So actually this, let me say, teams were observing according to the new zones of separations or zone of responsibility of each team. So Steinar pointed to team leaders. There are no new areas of responsibilities. And they were supposed to -- to report such data to headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And these are the same teams that are listed here in P68 on the --

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's why we can see -- I mean, Sibenik and other teams in spite of the fact that initially that were not their areas of responsibilities, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, go back to P98, these numbers, who ordered that this statistical compilation be put together? Was it the HRAT? Was it UNMO in Zagreb? Who ordered that. It's back on the screen. The usher put it back on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember the date. I do not remember the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ermolaev, could you -- the question was who ordered it. If Mr. Kehoe is interested to know when it was ordered --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, so if you could first focus on who did it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you don't know, tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. So first of all there was a meeting of civil affairs and Human Rights Watch, and I do believe that there was no Mr. Forand there because that was a new mission of the -- of the sector. I think that he was not present there. So -- and during several meetings we conducted, and according from Zagreb, I mean, the new, let me say, power in leading this process was United Nations Civil Affairs Office, and that's why the recommendation what UNMOs are supposed to do there were elaborated there, and then subsequently I just asked preparations, and when Steinar arrived. So the -- such a work started, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might have one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you note in this that it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, would you allow me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have now clearly explained that there were meetings and matters changed, et cetera, and that you said you started preparing and then Steinar arrived and then it started. I still do not know who instructed, who gave the order, to make this compilation. I know who prepared it. I know when it started. I know a lot, but not an answer to the question. If you know, please tell us. If you don't know, tell us as well. Or was it a body that ordered it, whatever it was, but ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So with the -- with the -- with any activity which we initiate and then implement is ordered by, in such particular case -- was authorised, let me say, and -- by UNMO headquarters Zagreb, and -- so we just -- this new functions are discussed, and Steinar was in contact with the chief military observer, and such a taskings, and on the basis how to do it, how to make it in a proper way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But the order, the final on the activity of the United Nations military observers is fully authorised and is done by our high command. I mean UNMO Zagreb, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You initiated it. It got the green light. That's from your command. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So that the proposals how do we plan it. When we conducted meetings with civil affairs and with Human Rights Watch we prepared our proposals as usual for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now -- I'm sorry. Now, sir, you noted in this P97 that 13.000 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can pull that back up, please, Madam Registrar. That would be P97.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You noted in this paragraph 1 that: "As of 13 September 1995, out of 18.232 houses and 24 villages and hamlets checked by UNMOs. "More than 13.600 houses have been completely or partially burnt/destroyed after Operation Storm."

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I'd just like to make a correction. It's actually 240 villages, not 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I apologise. I apologise. I stand corrected. It's absolutely right. It's 240 villages. I'm getting a little ahead of myself. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you noted for us during the course of your testimony yesterday that -- and it was yesterday, on page 2323, lines 16 to 18 -- excuse me, even starting at 13: "So the role of the UNMOs regarded to, if I properly got it, concerning human rights violations, that was not the proper mission I had there. You must clearly understand, so that is why we had subordinative function. And if and when we found something we reported it to human rights --" Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you participated in nightly meetings with the Human Rights Action Teams on a daily basis, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not personally myself every day, but there are at initial stage I participated in the first, but then there was our -- and then we attached some people there. I'm not quite sure that all the time, I mean the whole month or whenever, in the evening civil affairs meetings there was an UNMO representative. I'm not quite confident in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, do you remember Mr. Edward Flynn? He was a Prosecution witness here back on April the 11th, 2008, who was a human rights coordinator in Sector South.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And he testified on page 1314 and 1315 as follows, starting on 1314, line 24: "Question: At some point your HRAT teams had nightly meetings; is that correct? "Answer: Yes. "Question: As part of those nightly meetings, did representatives of the UNMOs, the UNMOs, attend the meetings? "Answer: Yes. "Question: Do you recall anyone specifically from UNMO who would attend the meetings? "Answer: May I -- excuse me, may I refer to my notes? "Question: Yes. "Answer: Sorry I'm having trouble locating that. All right. I remember Colonel Sethsun [phoen] being quite involved in these meetings and also Colonel Ermolaev." He may have had the rank wrong but Ermolaev. There was only one Ermolaev in Sector South; right?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Question at line 12 -- actually we can go down to line 16. "Question: Did the UNMOs ever appear at that HRAT evening meeting and tell you that they counted, let's say, 11.000 burnt houses? "Answer: No, not to my recollection. "Question: That number would have been something that you would have remembered; is that correct? "Answer: I think so." Mr. Ermolaev, why when you went to these meetings or why when UNMOs went to these meetings were they not reporting to the Human Rights Action Team coordinator Mr. Flynn the number of houses that were being burnt?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. So first of all I -- I do believe as him -- forgotten, you know, my rank and proper name, as well as I by the way forgot his. So we can see here a fact from UNMO HQ Zagreb side by me personally, and you can see an information HRAT SS, PAO SS, UNCIVPOL SS, I do not how can I confirm that I inform them. That means that they are immediately all adversat [phoen] which are here that they receive such a report. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So is it your testimony here that you, in fact, advised Mr. Flynn and the HRAT teams of the number of houses that you -- that the UNMOs counted as being burnt and destroyed? You informed him of that?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. We -- we see according to this paper which was, you know, we can see here that it was addressed to him. So I'm a little bit, you know, taken aback by hearing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let me turn to line 23 in the testimony of -- again on page 1315 of Mr. Flynn. "I know that the UNMOs were conducting a survey, and I know that their numbers were high. Again, as I say, when I refer to my own estimate my extent is to be on the conservative side. I don't recall, though, any discussions with regard to those numbers while I was there, those kinds of numbers."

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. No one could discuss those numbers till the entire final report was ready and because no one had any idea about the picture of what was going on in Sector South till the date when it was combined by officer in charge and issued. Secondly, Mr. Flynn, and we closely cooperated with him, was actively involved in his field activity. He has his deputies, Maria Teresa, whatever. We travelled with her as well a lot. So it might be there with there some chain of command, but it's strange to me to hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, let us continue on on 1316. Question line 3: "Let's discuss what you would discuss at an HRAT meeting at which UNMOs were present and if they counted 11.000 homes would that not be something that would be discussed at the evening meeting of HRAT? "Answer: Yes."

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "Question: So you're telling us at least through your time which is I believe you said through the 16th of September," by the way your report is the 13th of September, "no UNMO came to a meeting and said we've counted 11.000 burnt houses? "Answer: I only recall and I only reported on the sightings that have been made yet -- that day, and I don't recall that we discussed any information as you've described." Now --

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's this? I just cannot understand what --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is the testimony of Mr. Flynn.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ah, okay. Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Flynn was the person to whom you were supposed to be providing human rights information, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain to you with Mr. Flynn. It's a very good question you raised. Human rights team was mostly at least at this stage till 15th August when I was there, because then actually, you know, Steinar visited this meetings and I had no connections with him, I mean, direct connections with him. So that's why I cannot comment whether Steinar reported to him about or not. But returning back to person to whom we were supposed to be providing human rights information, so the chain of command and no one disclosed such chain of command as to report to UNMO headquarters Zagreb. Secondly, we -- you can see here that such a report is addressed to my commander, chief military observer, and information number one to chief civil affairs Sector South. So the chain of command was the same, but here with the information on the ground primarily he has only one car, and the only place where Mr. Flynn went to -- Flynn, when there was some reports about some killings or some episodes in cemetery and he spent there days, days, and weeks, and we put in line just expecting him to visit any other area where he was supposed to investigate. And he could not and never was interested in other operational activities of UNMOs or battalions because he was mostly concentrated on his main mission to conduct in-depth evaluation of these cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Ermolaev, let's move to another topic. The -- let me turn our attention to -- back to P111. Now -- I'm sorry. P111 is a situation report from 7 August 1995, and if we can turn our -- it doesn't have a pagination to it, but I do believe it is page 4 of this document. And if we go to the Jordbat AOR and just blow that up it notes there on the 07 -- "The 7th of August HV troops enter Uzelac with the grid number and then headed to Nablisi -- Nabulsi," excuse me, "with the same grid reference comment. HV troops are moving to the Bosnian border." Is that your comment, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. I never touched, you know, with my hands reports by battalions, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, HV troops as of the 7th were in fact moving into Bosnia, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You don't recall. Well, let's go to -- how many pages up. We go one, two, three -- four pages up, and it should be R1059163 is the ERN number. It should be part of the same report. Can we just go four and five pages up with the "Not be guaranteed," line at the top? It should be the next page. Okay. I'm sorry. Can you just ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. It seems to be page 8 of the document which was just on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Which is -- and ends with the ERN 9578 it appears.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I have a different ERN number on that. Thank you very much, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, on the top there it notes that: Sector South delegation, do you see that, "was told military and civil police took over control of Knin and that the last two brigades had left Knin on 6 August." Was that consistent with the information that you were receiving?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's according to this one. So it is clear that Sector South delegation was told, so -- I mean. So it's clear, I mean, for me that information received, not confirmed. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, without going through all these situation reports, over the next several weeks from the 6th and 7th of August, your UNMOs were tracking troop movements by the HV, weren't you? It might be quicker just to show you something. Let me show you P120, and we'll go to the first page of P120.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that -- you suggest that UNMOs were tracking Croatian troops' movements or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: By saying that. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: They were not?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, well let's go to this particular sheet, and I believe that P120 at the first page, this is in your highlights that you wrote. You see "Jordbat reported troop movements into Bosnia." If we go to the next page under -- the next page of that document under -- that's the -- next page under that document. If we could just about under little (a )which is UNMO headquarter patrol reported. We can read that. That reflects, for instance, in the second paragraph, a convoy of 15 military trucks with approximately 300 soldiers heading north. If we move down two paragraphs: "Ambulances four time minor HV vehicles with approximately 200 soldiers heading north probably towards Bosnia." That's P120. Let's go to P122.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, trust me I won't go through all of these. They'll speak for themselves. I'm just clarifying for -- adjusting the witness. I can certainly go through them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: P122 SMO assessment at the bottom of that page. This is 17 of August, 1995. SMO's assessment, "Continuation of HV troop build up in the eastern part of the sector indicates possible offensive towards the general area of Drvar with the grid reference. Most likely this is part of a larger operation." Now, where is Drvar, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, I would not like to comment on SMO's assessment Colonel Steinar and what he put down here and conclusions he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ermolaev, Mr. Kehoe has drawn our attention and to some extent your attention as well to what's written in sitreps. He has not put any further question in relation to that. The simple question he now puts to you, "Where is Drvar?" If you could tell us where it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah I cannot recollect exactly all the cities, you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well let me help you, sir. Isn't Drvar in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that I answered so far that I can recollect now at this stage and today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, I can go through more sitreps and cite them to you, sir, but I really don't have the time. Is it your testimony to this Chamber that the -- that the UNMOs were not tracking HV troop movements throughout August into September?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: So let's just return back to a question because you changed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm asking this question. I asked the question and you can just read it from the screen or I can repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: You changed it. Your first question was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, you asked a similar question, then you -- not exactly the same, then you put a lot of examples where apparently you find there was at least observation of troop movements, and then you put a question slightly differently phrased. The witness is not invited to at length comment on what the differences are, but the witness may draw our attention to the difference in the language you used and may also answer now this question, and if it's in every -- in any respect different from the previous question he may, although very briefly, explain where the differences are, not the full background of the differences. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry. Two sentences. So my answer is that the new taskings to ensure monitoring of the situation with humanitarian situation in the terrain, that was the new taskings to UNMOs, but no one can sold the main taskings of military observers in Knin or any other place, not to monitor military situation on the ground, because that's why they are called by the United Nations Security Council as United Nations Military Observer to observe military situation and that's why humanitarian taskings was a brand new for us. We were not trained to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, your testimony on -- yesterday on page 2291, you testified at line 15: "That was the primary mission of these negotiations, because we clearly understood that mandate we had terminated." And -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The only mandate you had at that point was to examine or surveil for human rights violations pursuant to the Sarinic-Akashi agreement. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely -- absolutely incorrect. And allow just United Nations structure of command to decide what to do and how to do. This is not our -- your and my area of responsibilities, what taskings should be tasked to the United Nations personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, if you said in your testimony yesterday that your mandate had terminated.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I can specify that the mandate to monitor zone of separation was physically finished because of events that took place, by saying that I mentioned zone of separation, just to be specific. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us pull up D28.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While waiting, you've still got five minutes, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, I want you to look at this. This is the Sarinic-Akashi agreement that was signed on 6th August, 1995, which refers to the continuing activities of the UN in what was -- in Sector South and Sector North. There is nothing in this agreement that allows UNMOs to monitor military movements of HV personnel and equipment, does it?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: This --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I can go to page 2 and read that as well.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: This we can see as addition to the mandate because UNCRO mandate no one cancelled. So that's why this in addition to the basic mandate for UNCRO activities in the area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So your testimony is that your mandate continued and then you got human rights violations examination on top of that, right?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wait a second. So we officially reported to the United Nations command. General Forand reported to UNCRO command Zagreb, as well as I reported through my chain of command, that we do consider that the presence of battalions of UNMOs in new surroundings and et cetera. So but we didn't officially receive any command from high command that we should stop our activity with its mandate which was signed by President Tudjman. That's very simple. If I got -- if I had got such an record, Terminate your activity and go home, I would have immediately withdrawn my UNMOs. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kehoe. Mr. Russo, any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Just a few brief questions if I could, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You could.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar could we please pull up Exhibit P147.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if we could please turn to page 7 of that document. I'm sorry, page 6. And if we could enlarge the top portion. Thank you. Mr. Ermolaev, you were asked questions with regard to this document, specifically questions regarding the passage which appears on the preceding page about the operational responsibility of General Cermak -- I'm sorry, the non-operational responsibility of General Cermak. I'd like to direct your attention to where it indicates at number 2: "As per the order of the Ministry of Defence, only the Generals Gotovina and Cermak can deal with the international organisations directly. All other official contacts have to pass through CALOs. Therefore it is not necessary for the international organisations to have the list of the names of the responsible and/or commanding officers of the Croatian army." Can you please explain to the Court, was there some effort on behalf of the UNMOs to determine who was responsible for doing what in Sector South?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, actually I never ask such a question, because from the very beginning, from my first meeting with Cermak and information as stated here, so to me, I mean, the main person who was -- whom we were dealing with and on all matters in Sector South, not only in Knin that fishing plant was opened, but about all situation in Knin, and we saw things everywhere which clearly confirm that he was in charge of at least all answers and all activities were done officially through Cermak, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. If we could please now bring up document D50. Mr. Ermolaev, if you will recall you were shown this document on cross-examination by I believe it was Mr. Cayley and this is document request from the Ministry of the Interior requesting to collect information on crimes which were occurring in Sector South. I'd like to ask you, did the Ministry of Interior ever contact you or other UNMOs to ask for the information which you were collecting at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never we were asked to present the first one when we were asked that was letter by General Cermak where he wrote that he doesn't know anything about such activities in the area of his responsibilities. So -- and repeatedly we asked, I mean, ourselves, I mean, whom we should address such questions if, for example, there are Serbs population found in some village. So who would take care of them? Who would provide them with food, with water. So partially UNMOs, as much as we could, we delivered it. We received rations from ICRC, delivered it to villages. Later on we started when United Nations CIVPOL gradually took over and later on as I already witnessed they started some joining operations of civilian police, with Croatian police, but that took place later on, I mean, in September, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the Croatian police ever seek to interview any of your UNMOs with regard to the observations regarding any of the crimes that they reported?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do not remember a case when they didn't interview with, and particularly, I mean, in such sensitive issues when UNMOs or international community, for example, German TV, when they were coming and, you know, seeing such violation of human rights, particularly burning of houses and et cetera, so immediately they were merely attacked rudely and physically by representatives of Croatian police, or if it was a mixed patrol. So depending on the place where they were also. I can say at least till the time I was there. I cannot say that -- for sure there were some places, and I want to make it clear where we didn't experience absolutely problems with, you know, Croatian police, yes. But there -- but in general, what I remember, so every day such reports were received.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I think you may have misunderstood my question --

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: -- Mr. Ermolaev. What I was attempting to find out is whether or not the Croatian police in conducting an investigation into any of the crimes which had been reported by your UNMOs, if they interviewed your UNMOs as witnesses to those crimes, as part of a Croatian police investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour I think there is a lack of foundation here. I think there has to be an establishment first that the UNMOs reported these directly to the Croatian police. It's my understanding that they went straight up the chain of command to Zagreb and that Zagreb came back to the local people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So they were two --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. One second. Yes. The lack of foundation would be only the reporting by the UNMOs, but the question, therefore, is now, Mr. Ermolaev, whether your UNMOs were ever interviewed by the Croatian police directly on events, including violations of human rights that were reported as witnesses of those events. Did the Croatian police ever come and say, "We'd like to interview Mr. A, Mr. B," or, "Please try to find out who witnessed it so that we can interview him"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Well, at least as I remember, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was misunderstood, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Madam Registrar if we can please pull up document number P63.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Ermolaev, you were asked a number of questions regarding who ordered the turning of survey regarding the burned houses and individuals left behind. I will ask you please to take a look at this document, first of all tell me if you recall ever seeing this document before. We'll start there.

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall this document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Okay. Looking at the date of the document, 17th August 1995, can you tell us who was the SMO at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIKHAIL ERMOLAEV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Steinar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Russo. Has the re-examination triggered any need for further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ermolaev, the Bench has no further questions for you. This means that this concludes your testimony. We'd like to thank you very much for coming and for your answers to the questions of the parties and of the Bench, and the Chamber wishes you not only a safe trip home again but also a timely trip home again so that you'll be in time to attend the celebration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, I think we have dealt with all the exhibits, so there's no need -- we have no open MFIs for this witness. Is there any procedural matter, any other procedural matter we have to address at this very moment? If not, we stand adjourned until Thursday, the 1st of May, 9.00 in the morning. Madam Registrar, is that the same courtroom? The same courtroom. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 1st day of May, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 25
